scope_gaps.note: Source tested a prompted procedure (written recall of earlier similar assignments plus two linking questions) in one ~1-hour computer assignment for psychology undergraduates with 1- or 2-week deadlines; the title states the advice for any new task and does not name those conditions.

Study 4 participants described how far before deadlines they typically finished similar assignments and answered two prompted questions (date if they finished as early as typical; a scenario for finishing at the typical time). The item's steps (check how long the earlier task took, write down how it relates, then set the deadline) are an editorial simplification, which the item itself says (W praktyce#2). Not tested outside this lab task.

Linking was induced by instructions to the assigned recall-relevant group, not chosen by participants; effect is a group-level result. Participants in that group seldom reported using past experiences in their listed thoughts (12.5%, Table 4), so the mechanism is not shown.
The item compares only the recall-relevant and control groups; the source also has a recall-only group (38.1%) that did not differ from control.
The paper reports five studies; the item rests on Study 4 only. The sentence says 'studentów'; the source specifies undergraduate psychology students (46 men, 77 women).
